title: How to use past papers
examples: Should I do all the past papers or just a few?
How do I use the marking scheme when I finish?
What is the best way to keep track of my mistakes?

explain.say: First we will look at doing timed papers under exam conditions.

items: Set a timer for the paper duration
Stop when the time runs out

explain.say: Next we need to understand how to use the official marking scheme correctly.

explain.say: Remember to review your mistakes after marking every paper you complete.
For a real life example think about studying for a big test.
A common mistake is forgetting to time yourself during the practice session.

faq.q: How often should I do past papers?
faq.a: You should aim to do them regularly as you get closer to the exam date. Doing them too often without revision time is not helpful. You could also ask, 'What is a good schedule for practice?' or 'Should I do one every week?'
asks: What is the frequency of doing past papers?

faq.q: Do I need to use the marking scheme for every question?
faq.a: Yes, you should look at the marking scheme to understand exactly what the examiners are looking for. It shows you how marks are allocated. You might also ask, 'Is the marking scheme important?' or 'How do I use the mark scheme?'
asks: Should I check the mark scheme?
What is the purpose of the marking guide?

faq.q: What should I write in my error log?
faq.a: You should write down the topic, the mistake you made, and the correct way to solve it. This helps you see patterns in your mistakes. Another way to ask is, 'What information goes in the log?'
asks: What to record in the error log?
How should I structure my mistake notes?

faq.q: If I get a low mark, does that mean I am bad at the subject?
faq.a: No, getting a low mark just shows you exactly where you need to study more. It is a guide, not a final judgment of your ability. You can ask, 'Is a low grade bad?', or 'What does a low mark mean?'
asks: What is the purpose of a low mark?

faq.q: Should I only focus on the topics I find difficult?
faq.a: No, you must practice all topics to ensure you are prepared everywhere. Sometimes you forget the easy things when you are under pressure. You could ask, 'Should I ignore the easy topics?'
asks: Do I only study hard topics?
Is it okay to skip easy topics?

facts: Timed papers help you manage your time effectively during the actual exam.
The marking scheme tells you the exact criteria for gaining marks.
An error log helps you study your mistakes, not just the correct answers.
Practicing under timed conditions reduces exam anxiety.

quiz.say: If you spend too much time on one difficult question, what skill are you neglecting?

options.show: Only answering the easiest questions first.
options.say: Only answering the easiest questions first.

options.show: Spending all your time on one question.
options.say: Spending all your time on one question.

options.show: Completing all sections within the time limit.
options.say: Completing all sections within the time limit.

quiz.why: The correct answer is right because time management means allocating time fairly across all parts of the paper.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it feels safe, but you might miss marks on harder questions.
wrong.1: This is tempting because it saves time, but it means you are not practicing your weakest areas.
wrong.2: This is tempting because you want to get it perfect, but it leaves no time for other questions.

quiz.say: When checking your work against the mark scheme, what should you focus on?

options.show: Only checking if the final number is correct.
options.say: Only checking if the final number is correct.

options.show: Comparing your answer to a friend's.
options.say: Comparing your answer to a friend's.

options.show: Matching your answer structure to the required format.
options.say: Matching your answer structure to the required format.

quiz.why: The correct answer is right because examiners mark both correct content and how well you present it.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it is fast, but it ignores marks for showing your working steps.
wrong.1: This is tempting because it gives instant feedback, but it doesn't show you the official grading standard.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it seems unnecessary, but it means you don't know what the examiner expects.

quiz.say: If you keep writing down 'Forgot to carry the one' in your error log, what does this show?

options.show: You should just ignore that mistake.
options.say: You should just ignore that mistake.

options.show: A consistent arithmetic error needing practice.
options.say: A consistent arithmetic error needing practice.

options.show: You are bad at math generally.
options.say: You are bad at math generally.

options.show: You need to change subjects entirely.
options.say: You need to change subjects entirely.

quiz.why: The correct answer is right because logging patterns helps you focus your revision efforts precisely.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it is easier, but ignoring it means you will make the same mistake next time.
wrong.2: This is tempting because it feels like a big problem, but it is only one small, fixable error.
wrong.3: This is tempting because the mistake feels huge, but it just needs targeted practice.
